It allows a 0.04 EPA per dropback [dc1] on 358 pass plays [dc2] and a 40.2% success rate [dc3], so Indianapolis should expect efficient throws rather than only chunk plays. The run defense has been better, at -0.05 EPA per carry [dc4] and 42.7% success [dc5], so IND can lean on the run to set up play action. Explosive passing is the threat: 10.1% of pass plays gain 20 or more yards [dc6], while runs gain 10 or more only 7.8% of the time [dc7]. Houston's red zone defense is weak, allowing touchdowns on 68.0% of trips [dc8] over 25 drives [dc9], but IND has scored on 61.5% of its own red zone drives [dc10], so the matchup favors stretching the field early and cashing in inside the 20. IND has allowed a 17.8% pressure proxy [dc17] and a 7.1% sack rate [dc18]. Protection calls and quick game against the blitz will matter more than anything else in this matchup.
